content.value_statement: Go teams need consistent patterns for concurrency, interfaces, testing, and service structure. This skill provides focused guidance for idiomatic Go implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Design worker pools, pipelines, channel flows, and cancellation-aware goroutine lifecycles.
Create small Go interfaces, dependency injection boundaries, and functional option patterns.
Use Go generics for constraints, reusable collections, map operations, and typed channels.
Plan table-driven tests, subtests, benchmarks, fuzz tests, and race detector coverage.
Structure Go modules, internal packages, build tags, Makefiles, Dockerfiles, and configuration.
Review Go code for error wrapping, context propagation, documentation, and idiomatic formatting.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automatic execution of local Go tools.
It cannot verify runtime performance without benchmarks or profiler output from the project.
It does not replace human review for API design, concurrency safety, or production rollout.
It may need project constraints before choosing storage, transport, or deployment patterns.

use_cases.title: Implement Concurrent Workers
use_cases.description: Design goroutine lifecycles, context cancellation, channel buffering, and tests for a new background worker.

use_cases.title: Review Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess package layout, interface boundaries, configuration, and error handling before a Go service release.

use_cases.title: Improve Go Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Plan table-driven tests, benchmarks, fuzz tests, race checks, and mocks for critical Go packages.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Idiomatic Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Use golang-pro to implement this Go function. Explain package structure, error handling, and tests in plain language: [describe function].

prompt_templates.title: Add Concurrency Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use golang-pro to add bounded concurrency to this workflow. Include cancellation, backpressure, error propagation, and race detector test guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Go Microservice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use golang-pro to design a Go microservice for [domain]. Include interfaces, package layout, gRPC or REST boundaries, configuration, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Performance and Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use golang-pro to review this Go package for API boundaries, allocation pressure, benchmark coverage, context use, and concurrency risks.

output_examples.input: Design a worker pool for image processing.
output: A worker-pool plan with bounded concurrency, cancellation behavior, backpressure, error propagation, and shutdown rules.
A focused test plan covering success paths, cancellation, worker failures, and race detector checks.

output_examples.input: Review tests for a Go package.
output: A coverage review that identifies missing edge cases, table-driven scenarios, benchmarks, fuzz targets, and mock boundaries.
Prioritized recommendations for improving confidence without creating brittle tests.
A package structure with command entry points, internal packages, domain boundaries, configuration, and deployment files.
Guidance for dependency direction, exported APIs, build tags, and release metadata.

best_practices: Provide current package structure, Go version, and relevant constraints before asking for implementation.
Ask for tests and benchmarks with the implementation when behavior or performance matters.
Request context cancellation and error handling details for any blocking or concurrent operation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for goroutines without defining ownership, cancellation, and shutdown behavior.
Do not request large generic abstractions when simple concrete types meet the requirement.
Do not skip race, fuzz, or benchmark guidance for shared state and hot paths.

faq.question: What Go versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Go 1.21 and newer patterns, while also covering features introduced in Go 1.18.

faq.question: Can it help with gRPC services?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide service boundaries, context use, interfaces, testing, and project layout for gRPC or REST services.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent controls any local command execution.

faq.question: Can it review existing Go code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant files and goals, then ask for review of correctness, idioms, tests, and performance.

faq.question: Does it cover generics?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes constraints, type parameters, generic collections, generic interfaces, and union constraints.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes context propagation, explicit errors, testing, benchmarks, configuration, and maintainable module structure.
